summary: Remove the unrelated 36/47 reference from the church-naming example.
rationale: The supplied 36/47 has a sultan going to a mosque to pray, not i=ʕito ... Mōr Barṣawmo; 11/176 does match the inherited example.

summary: New box Imperativ: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (JTM 3.2/42)

data.turoyo: <...> "Mṣalawu lani d klayṭənxu, ibaʕu lani d kəbʕi u qaṭlaṯxu." <...>
data.translation: Betet für die, die euch verfluchen, und denen, die euch töten wollen, <...>

rationale: New Imperativ box; m-prefixed plural and l-marked prayer beneficiaries.

summary: New box Imperativ: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (PrS 60/120)

data.turoyo: Qrele laʕ ʕəbugre, omər :"Ramḥəl hušabo yo, itoxu li ʕito, ṣalawu, dlo man niše, ṭro fayši an niše."
data.translation: Darauf liess er den Mäusen befehlen: "Morgen ist Sonntag, da kommt alle zur Kirche, um zu beten, aber ohne die Weiber, die lasst zu Hause bleiben."

rationale: New Imperativ box; unprefixed ṣalawu contrasts with JTM Mṣalawu.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (44/130)

data.turoyo: Haṯe aṯyo w brəkla quma di dawmo w mṣalela w ṭləbla mu qadišo di zyara w məlla: "Ya qadišo! Koṭəlbono menux."
data.translation: Die Tante kam, kniete vor dem baume nieder, betete, bat den Heiligen des Wallfahrtsortes und sprach: "O Heiliger! Ich bitte dich."

rationale: Fills Preterit sense 1, and supplies the feminine L-agent -la.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (Talay 1/178)

data.turoyo: W mṣaleli, maṭino lalye d ḥamšo, koṯe komər: "Ṣafro nfaq Šəmʕun kifo men beṯ asire, wa b lilyo nfal šəšloṯo men iḏay Fawlus w b lilyo qore... da ḥṭiṯo."
data.translation: Ich betete und gelangte - es war die Nacht zu Donnerstag, - (zu der Stelle) wo es heißt: Am Morgen verließ Simon Petrus das Gefängnis, und in der Nacht fielen die Handschellen von der Hand des Paulus und in der Nacht ruft er ... der Sünde.

rationale: Fills Preterit sense 1 to five; first-person L-agent in liturgical reading.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (JTM 1.3/9)

data.turoyo: <...> u qašo kəmṣale ʕal i ṭlamṯo du laḥmano, w kəmmi əšmo d qole lašan Aloho, w bəṯr kəmmənne: "Twarulla."
data.translation: Der Priester segnet diesen Brotfladen, man singt einige religiöse Lieder, und dann sagt man zu ihnen: Brecht (den Fladen)!

rationale: Fills Infectum sense 1; nonhuman target of prayer with ʕal, without deriving a new sense from German segnet.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (MAC NE interview 1/8)

data.turoyo: Ádyawma, dəmṣalyono bgawa—oballa nahire, mṣalina bgawa—aṯyono qəm raġla di+Ndaṯalo, hawxa.
data.translation: Today, in order to pray inside it—I give her candles, we pray inside it—I came to the foot of the Theotokos, like so.

rationale: Fills Infectum sense 1 to five and distinguishes feminine first-person mṣalyono from Part act.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (JL 5.10/9)

data.turoyo: B lalyo, fəlge=d-lalyo, qaymiwayna li=ṣluṯo, mṣaliwayna i=ṣluṯo du=ḥašo, <...>
data.translation: (Jede) Nacht, utll Mitternacht, standen wir auf zum Gebet, beteten das Gebet der Karwoche, <...>

rationale: Fills Infectum-wa sense 1; recurrent prayer with a cognate object. Edition typo utll is retained.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (JTM 3.2/14)

data.turoyo: Kətwulle ḥasyo du čaġawo, lə kuḏaʕno əšme, saləq bi mədde du ḥarabano kule fayəš ʕal i goro, duʕewo, buxewo, ṣuyamwo w mṣalewo qm Aloho, Aloho d oṯe bi raḥme ʕal u šaʕb da mšiḥoye, d xulṣi w u mede d fayəš d lə məqṭoli.
data.translation: Sie hatten damals einen Bischof, dessen Namen ich nicht weiß, der stieg auf das Dach und blieb dort den ganzen Krieg über, er flehte, weinte, fastete und betete zu Gott, Gott möge Erbarmen mit dem Volk der Christen haben, damit sie entkämen und die, die noch übrig waren, nicht auch noch getötet würden.

rationale: Fills Infectum-wa sense 1; prayer qm Aloho in a sustained wartime sequence.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (MAC NE interview 1/3)

data.turoyo: <...> Hawxa mbelan ʕumran, ṣawmo ŭ ṣluṯo, mṣalíwayna, li+ʕito əzzáwayna, əḏʕíwayna bi+qima di+ʕito, du+qašo. <...>
data.translation: We spent our life in this way, fasting and prayer, we would pray, we would go to church, we would know the value of the church, of the priest.

rationale: Fills Infectum-wa sense 1 to five; MAC lifetime habit with explicit first-person plural.

summary: example for sense 1 in Part act. (JTM 3.1/23)

data.turoyo: U ḥasyo u lalyo w u imomo ṣayomo mṣalyono, əzzewo w əṯewo ʕal qarʕe du qadišo.
data.translation: Der Bischof fastete und betete Tag und Nacht, er ging immer wieder auf das Dach der Kirche.

rationale: Fills Part act. sense 1 with duration and an explicit bishop subject.

summary: example for sense 1 in Part act. (JTM 3.2/16)

data.turoyo: <...> bale hənne miṯe mu kafno, ṣayome, mṣalyone w baxoye w šapərza, Aloho mhawən aʕlayye.
data.translation: Dabei waren sie halbtot vor Hunger, sie fasteten, beteten und waren in einem elenden Zustand, Gott sei ihnen gnädig.

rationale: Fills Part act. sense 1 with plural predication.

summary: All securely identified Turoyo tokens continue II.1 beten, Gottesdienst abhalten; no new numbered sense. German segnen in the bread and clothes rituals describes the effect of prayer, while the Turoyo ʕal construction is already represented at 40/30.

Valency: unexpressed prayer content is common; ṣluṯo can be a zero-marked cognate object (JL 5.10/2, /9; 66/60; 94/33) or resumed by -la (68/45). Divine addressee m Aloho (24/2), qm Aloho (JTM 3.2/14), beneficiaries l- or lašan-, and language b səryoyo are distinct from L-marked Preterit agents (JTM 1.3/12).

Infectum covers ongoing, habitual, purposive and prospective prayer; Infectum-wa presents recurrent past practice; Part act. occurs in durable devotion and plural coordinated predicates. Detransitive kmiṣale at 11/75 suppresses the human officiant with church location bənne.

The Imperativ has ṣalawu in PrS and Mṣalawu in JTM; do not silently regularize either. Feminine first-person dəmṣalyono in MAC NE interview 1/8 is an Infectum purpose clause, distinct from the Part act. mṣalyono at 11/75.

Duplicate citations were not re-added (JL 19.6/17; 40/30; PrS 56/5). Reader questions claiming a missing translation at MAC NE interview 1/23 are obsolete for this supplied input, which contains the clauses.
No independently lexicalized idiom is established: praying a prayer and praying over ritual targets remain under sense 1.
Identify mmaṣalle at JTM 1.1/84 from its paradigm: is the milk-processing verb a separate ṣly/ṣll or mṣl root? No technical sense has been added.
Reconcile inherited PrS 151/37 with input PrS 56/5; these reproduce the same prayer/fasting sentence but may use different reference systems.

Confirm singular Imperativ Ṣalay at PrS 60/118 and the relation between ṣalawu and JTM Mṣalawu. The German confession clause at /118 does not match the direct request “pray over our heads”; it is not quoted as an example.
Resolve 69/275: Adlalyo kəmṣaleno lacks the negation and “here” present in the German. Confirm gəmṣaləṭ spelling at 69/272 and the plural -ən alongside ṣaymi at PrS 56/13.
The inherited 40/30 English has “a prayed”; check the editorial source before correcting its wording. Quoted Syriac nṣale (94/41) is excluded from the Turoyo paradigm.
Correct the noun in “uttered a prayed”
rationale: After the article a, the intended noun is prayer. The cited verse has mṣalele ʕal riši, translated betete er über meinem haupte.

summary: ʕal marks prayer targets including bread, clothes, a bridal couple, a deceased person and a chick. These ritual participant extensions do not require a separate blessing sense.
